metadata.title: Peculiarities of the higher education development in a blended learning environment
metadata.venue: RPGE– Revista on line de Política e Gestão Educacional

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses secondary data from TALIS 2018 (OECD, 2019) collected via a teacher questionnaire administered to higher education teachers in France and the Netherlands. The manuscript reports sample sizes by country and descriptive distributions, but it does not report any use of TALIS sampling weights or replicate weights in the analysis. The reported inferential method is Pearson correlation at the 1% significance level, which is not a survey-weighted complex-sample modeling workflow in the text. Therefore, the analysis should be treated as unweighted (or at least weight usage is not documented), and results may not fully reflect population-representative estimates under TALIS’s complex sampling design.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables in this study are teachers’ questionnaire responses about ICT training inclusion, readiness, and professional development impacts, which are not cognitive achievement scores with TALIS Plausible Values. TALIS teacher questionnaires are typically analyzed as Likert-style or categorical survey items rather than PV-based achievement scales, so PV handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling is not described, but the paper reports “No answer” categories in tables, suggesting that nonresponse may have been treated as an explicit response option rather than through a documented imputation/deletion procedure.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Secondary TALIS 2018 teacher survey data were used for France and the Netherlands. The analytic sample consists of 7,823 higher education teachers (France: 4,435; Netherlands: 3,388) who responded to questionnaire items about inclusion of ICT skills and ICT use in formal education and professional development, readiness to use ICT in teaching, and characteristics of the professional development activity with the greatest positive impact. The manuscript reports “No answer” proportions for several readiness and inclusion items, but it does not specify additional exclusion rules (e.g., complete-case only) or any further filtering beyond using the TALIS teacher questionnaire responses for the specified countries.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018 teacher survey data were used for France, the study leveraged Gender, Teaching work experience (years), Highest education level (ISCED) to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This paper analyzes secondary TALIS 2018 teacher questionnaire data for France and the Netherlands to describe higher education teachers’ reported inclusion of blended-learning-relevant components and ICT skills in formal education and professional development, and to examine associations among these questionnaire components. The study reports descriptive proportions (e.g., 50.0% report inclusion of blended-learning teaching components in formal education; 48.4% report inclusion of ICT use elements in further learning activities; 28.9% are “not at all” ready and 36.6% “somewhat” ready for ICT use in teaching). It also reports Pearson correlation results at the 1% level, including a strong negative association between formal education components in blended learning and teachers’ readiness for blended learning (−0.626) and between teacher preparation for ICT use and readiness for ICT use (−0.646). No machine learning models are trained or evaluated; therefore, there are no predictive performance metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) to report. Limitations include the absence of documented missing-data handling and the lack of explicit survey-weight usage in the analysis. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an empirical descriptive/correlation study using TALIS 2018 teacher questionnaire items, not a machine-learning predictive modeling paper. As a result, fields related to ML techniques and PV-based achievement prediction are not populated, and main_findings is left empty because the schema requires StructuredFinding rows only for distinct ML target variables with predictive metrics.
